The chosen mechanism is implemented with tests or documented as the process, in the owning repos
A core PR that bumps the version without site support is demonstrably refused or flagged before it reaches deploy
context: Program: autogen-issues-decisions-20261018 (decisions D1-D11 and guardrails G1-G12; read it first). description:
Re-homed scope. On 2026-10-17 three site deploys failed 'Explorer read-model version 16 expected, got 17. The core bundle's explorer/contract.json no longer matches explorer/scripts/explorer-build-contract.mjs; update the Explorer for the new contract' because core bumped the read-model version before the site accepted it. The gate worked; the cost was hours of undeployed site content and an incident. The batch only gives the failure a named class (site deploy reporter item). Preventing the ordering problem needs a design choice (site accepts N and N+1 during a transition, a core CI check against the site's accepted versions, or a documented release order) that was not decided in the owner dialog.
Work when taken: compare the options with evidence from the two repos, decide the smallest, and implement it.
